title: Does AI rate through the cycle? — reproducibility artifact
description:
Reproducibility artifact for the Finance Research Letters article Does AI rate through the cycle? Procyclicality in credit assessment — a controlled measurement of procyclicality in large-language-model credit assessment. Firm fundamentals are held byte-identical across an ordered five-point macroeconomic-severity axis and a matched credit-irrelevant placebo axis, so any rating movement is procyclical by construction.

The frozen dataset covers 7 models (including two frontier models) × 4 prompt framings × 80 synthetic firms × the severity and placebo axes, with five replicate seeds for four models and two for the remaining three, re-measured 2.5 months apart to separate replication noise from version drift: 61 capture files and 99,366 rows, each file carrying a SHA-256 freeze receipt. A real-firm arm repeats the design on 80 companies built from public SEC company facts, with a credit-irrelevant placebo and a contamination and issuer-recall battery.

The analysis regenerates the cyclicality coefficient (notches per severity step) with firm-clustered bootstrap 95% CIs, the boom-to-recession swing, the downside/upside asymmetry and its bootstrapped ratio intervals, the Amato–Furfine ordered-probit null, the log-probability expected-notch estimator, the placebo-adjusted (net) coefficient, the through-the-cycle and “be stable” instruction contrasts, default-probability retention against the Basel PD floor, TOST equivalence tests, Holm-corrected multiplicity, and synthetic-versus-real distributional overlap.

Reproduction is offline, deterministic and free: bash reproduce.sh verifies every freeze receipt and the frozen pre-registration, regenerates the results and requires them to match byte-for-byte. Python 3.10+ is required. Live model capture needs vendor API keys and is intentionally excluded from the reproduction path.
notes: Code released under MIT (see LICENSE); data, analysis outputs and text under CC-BY-4.0 (both stated in LICENSE). Working copy: https://github.com/samirrc2/Does-AI-rate-through-the-cycle---Procyclicality-in-credit-assessment. Cite the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21864041, which resolves to the newest version. Live-capture SDKs (openai, google-genai) are not required to reproduce results from the frozen data.
